title: Open images of representable etale morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E,F$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an algebraic space $Z$, let $|Z|$ be its field-valued point classes: maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ for fields $K$, identified when they agree over a common field extension. Give $|Z|$ the topology in which a subset is open if its inverse image in an etale scheme atlas is open. An open subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable by open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Open subspaces of $F$ correspond bijectively, preserving inclusion, to open subsets of $|F|$. Let $q:E\to F$ be representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its point image is open and corresponds to an open subspace $I\subseteq F$; $q$ factors through $I$, and $E\to I$ is representable surjective etale. For every morphism of algebraic spaces $g:G\to F$, the image open subspace of $E\times_FG\to G$ is $I\times_FG$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $|E|$ is quasi-compact (every open covering has a finite subcover), then $|I|$ is quasi-compact. For any algebraic space $Z$, $|Z|$ is quasi-compact if and only if $Z$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme.

proof.text: First record the point calculation. For maps $A\to B$ and $C\to B$ of algebraic spaces, equality of the images of $a\in|A|$ and $c\in|C|$ means that representatives agree over a common field $M$. The two maps from $\operatorname{Spec}M$ therefore give a point of $A\times_BC$ by the sheaf fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Conversely a point of that product gives such equal images. Consequently $\operatorname{im}(|A\times_BC|\to|C|)=|C|\times_{|B|}\operatorname{im}(|A|\to|B|)$, where the right side means inverse image as a subset. In particular a representable morphism is surjective on all scheme base changes if and only if it is surjective on point classes: one direction tests a field-valued point and chooses a point in the surjective scheme fibre; for the other, apply the calculation to each scheme $C\to B$.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), explicit common-field proof; Tag 03H5 (lemma-characterize-surjective), same scheme-test argument for representable maps

proof.text: Use [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] for atlas-independent quotient topologies, point-surjective scheme atlases, continuity of every scheme-source map and openness of every etale scheme-source map. Every morphism $f:A\to B$ is continuous: for an atlas $p:U\to A$ and open $O\subseteq|B|$, the inverse image of $f^{-1}O$ in $U$ is $(fp)^{-1}O$, which is open, so the quotient topology applies. An open subspace $J\hookrightarrow A$ is injective on point classes, since equality after a common extension reflects through a monomorphism. For an atlas $U\to A$, its pullback $U_J\to U$ is an open subscheme by the definition of open subspace [def-weil-open-immersion]. The map $U_J\to J$ is a point-surjective etale atlas by base change [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Thus $|J|$ is an open subset of $|A|$: its inverse image is precisely $U_J$ by step 1. Its topology is the subspace topology, because a subset of $U_J$ is open there exactly when it is open in $U$, and both atlas maps define the quotient topologies.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), quotient topology and scheme-source openness; open-immersion restriction in Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces)

proof.text: Let $O\subseteq|F|$ be open. Choose a scheme atlas $p:U\to F$ and put $V=p^{-1}O\subseteq U$. Apply [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation]: $R=U\times_FU$ is an etale equivalence relation and $F=U/R$ as an fppf sheaf quotient. Since $ps=pt$, the open subschemes $s^{-1}V$ and $t^{-1}V$ of $R$ coincide. Their common value is $R_V=V\times_U R\times_U V$: membership in one inverse image forces membership in the other. The maps $R_V\to V$ are the base changes of $s,t$ along $V\hookrightarrow U$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. On $T$-points this is the restriction of the equivalence relation to $V(T)$, so it is again an equivalence relation.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), proof: invariant open V and restricted relation; spaces.tex Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to $R_V\rightrightarrows V$. Its quotient $J=V/R_V$ is an algebraic space and $V\to J$ is representable surjective etale. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens] to $V\hookrightarrow U$ and $R\rightrightarrows U$ to obtain a representable open immersion $J\hookrightarrow F$. Its hypotheses hold: the projections of $R$ are surjective etale by step 3; $V\hookrightarrow U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; these maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Identify $J$ with its subfunctor image. By step 1 the map $|V|\to|J|$ is surjective, so $|J|=p(|V|)=O$, the last equality using the point-surjectivity of $p$ and $V=p^{-1}O$. This constructs an open subspace for every open subset.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inverse construction via spaces.tex Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens) and Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation)

proof.text: If $J_1,J_2\subseteq F$ are open subspaces and $|J_1|\subseteq|J_2|$, test any map $T\to J_1$ from a scheme. The open immersion $T\times_FJ_2\to T$ has every point of $T$ in its image by step 1. An open immersion with full underlying image is an isomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Hence $T\to F$ factors uniquely through $J_2$. Uniqueness makes these factorizations natural in $T$, proving $J_1\subseteq J_2$ as subfunctors. The converse follows by taking point classes. Thus step 4 gives the required inclusion-preserving bijection, including uniqueness of the open subspace with a given underlying open subset.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), injectivity and preservation/reflection of inclusion; Tag 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace) argument written out

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $p:U\to E$. The composite $qp:U\to F$ is representable etale: after any scheme test $T\to F$, $E\times_FT$ is a scheme etale over $T$, and $U\times_FT\to E\times_FT$ is the scheme base change of the representable etale atlas $p$; composition is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The atlas existence and its point-surjectivity are supplied by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Apply the scheme-source openness clause of that same node to $qp$ to see that $\operatorname{im}|q|=\operatorname{im}|qp|$ is open. Steps 4-5 give its unique corresponding open subspace $I\subseteq F$.

source.place: Tag 03IR (lemma-etale-open), reduce to a scheme atlas and use Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points)

proof.text: The pullback $E_I=E\times_FI\to E$ is an open immersion: on every scheme test it is a scheme base change of the defining open immersion for $I$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Step 1 gives $|E_I|=|E|$, so step 5 identifies this open subspace with $E$ itself. This gives the factorization $q=j\circ q_I$. For a scheme $T\to I$, the monomorphism $I\hookrightarrow F$ identifies $E\times_IT=E\times_FT$ by their universal properties. This scheme is etale over $T$ by the hypothesis on $q$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The point map $|E|\to|I|$ is surjective by the choice of $I$, so step 1 proves surjectivity on every such scheme test. Thus $q_I$ is representable surjective etale.

source.place: Tag 03IE (lemma-factor-through-open-subspace) and Tag 06NF (lemma-etale-image-open), factorization and scheme-test proof, now for representable E to F

proof.text: For any $g:G\to F$, the sheaf product $E\times_FG$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its projection is representable etale: each scheme test $T\to G$ identifies its pullback with $E\times_FT\to T$, which is etale by the hypothesis on $q$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Step 1 gives its point image as $|g|^{-1}(|I|)$. The pullback $I\times_FG\to G$ is an open subspace by the scheme-test definition [def-weil-open-immersion] and has exactly this same point subset, again by step 1. Uniqueness in step 5 therefore identifies it with the image open subspace of $E\times_FG\to G$. No surjectivity, flatness or finite-type hypothesis on $g$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), apply the explicit point calculation and uniqueness of open subspaces

proof.text: The map $|E|\to|I|$ is continuous by step 2 and surjective by step 7. An open cover of $|I|$ therefore pulls back to an open cover of $|E|$; a finite subcover upstairs gives a finite subcover downstairs. This proves the quasi-compactness of $|I|$ when $|E|$ is quasi-compact. The identical finite-subcover argument proves that any representable surjective etale map $A\to Z$ from a quasi-compact scheme makes $|Z|$ quasi-compact, using continuity from step 2 and point-surjectivity from step 1.

source.place: Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), continuous-surjection direction, with the finite-subcover argument explicit

proof.text: Conversely suppose $|Z|$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] choose an atlas $p:A\to Z$ with $A=\coprod_{a\in D}A_a$ and all $A_a$ affine. The components are open subschemes by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each composite $A_a\to Z$ is representable etale, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] on scheme tests, and its point image is open by the scheme-source openness clause of the atlas node. These images cover $|Z|$; select finitely many that still cover. Let $A'$ be the union of the selected components, an open subscheme of $A$. Each component is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $A'$ is quasi-compact: restrict any open cover to each of the finitely many components and unite their finite subcovers. The restriction $A'\to Z$ remains representable etale, since its scheme base changes are an open immersion followed by an etale scheme map, again using the composition node. It is point-surjective by construction, hence representably surjective by step 1. If $Z$ is empty the finite selection may be empty and $A'$ is the empty quasi-compact scheme, so the argument includes this case.

source.place: Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), choose a quasi-compact open of the atlas; Tag 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), affine refinement

lean.statement: theorem etale_open_image {S : Scheme.{u}} (E F : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : E ⟶ F) (hq : IsEtale q.hom.hom) : IsOpen (pointImage q.hom.hom) ∧ ∃ A : OpenSubspace F, pointImage q.hom.hom = pointImage A.val.ι ∧ (∃ qI : E.obj.obj ⟶ A.val.toFunctor, qI ≫ A.val.ι = q.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale qI ∧ IsSurjective qI) ∧ (∀ (G : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : G ⟶ F), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (A.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι ∧ pointImage (Limits.pullback.snd q.hom g.hom).hom = pointImage (A.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι) ∧ (CompactSpace (Point E.obj.obj) → CompactSpace (Point A.val.toFunctor))
